Status:

milestones.note: Wisconsin Electric filed the Engineering Plan for docket 6630-CE-319 with the commission in October 2026.

Capacity (MW).note:
Capacity:
- Open the Fox North Engineering Plan at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=614115 and go to page 1-1, section 1.1 Proposed New Generating Unit. The first paragraph says a one-on-one combined cycle facility 'with a capacity of approximately 750 megawatts'.
- The memorandum at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=615110 repeats 'a new 750 megawatt (MW) natural gas fired combined cycle generating facility'. This matches the 750.0 MW now in the database.

Fuel.note:
Fuel:
- Open the Fox North Engineering Plan at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=614115 and go to page 1-1, section 1.1 Proposed New Generating Unit. The plan calls it a 'natural gas fired one-on-one (1x1) combined cycle generating facility'. Section 2.2.1 says the combustion turbine is 'fueled by natural gas'.

Turbine/Engine Technology.note:
Technology:
- Open the Fox North Engineering Plan at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=614115 and go to page 1-1, section 1.1 Proposed New Generating Unit. It says 'natural gas fired one-on-one (1x1) combined cycle generating facility' with one combustion turbine, one heat recovery steam generator and one steam turbine.

Equipment Manufacturer/Model.note:
Equipment:
- Open the Fox North Engineering Plan at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=614115 and go to page 1-1, section 1.1 Proposed New Generating Unit. The sentence 'a power island supplied by GE consisting of a single 7HA.03 combustion turbine generator' names the model.
- The engineering plan writes GE. GEM records the maker's current name, GE Vernova.
- Section 2.2.1 puts the combustion turbine generator at about 460 MW, and the steam turbine generator is about 306 MW.

Start year.note:
Start year:
- Open https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=614115 and go to section 4.0 Project Schedule. It says 'Wisconsin Electric anticipates commercial operation of the Project by Q4 2032' and 'Project construction is anticipated to begin in Q2 2029'.
- The 2032 start year matches the database. The human adds a new scheduled event for 2032 with Source Year 2026, never changes an existing one.

Backup Power.note:
Backup Power:
- Open https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=614115 and go to section 2.3.15 Emergency / Standby Generator(s). It says the project will include 'two natural gas-fired backup generators', one for safe shutdown loads and one for the fire pump.
- These are small auxiliary generators, not a backup fleet that stands in for grid power. The combined cycle unit supplies routine power, so Backup Power stays no.
